Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2148); Zacharias (i.e. Zechariah), the name of two Israelites:--Zacharias.
BiblicalUsage: Zacharias is Zechariah, the priest who becomes the father of John the Baptist. In Luke 1:5 he is "a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia," and in Luke 1:12, when the angel appears, "he was troubled, and fear fell upon him." Matthew 23:35 names another Zechariah, "Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar," a murdered prophet whose blood Jesus lays at the charge of his generation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two Zachariases in these verses hold the whole story together. I hold that the old priest in Luke 1:5 who prayed for a son and the murdered prophet of Matthew 23:35 both point to a God who hears prayers and who does not forget shed blood.
